title: Finalize Dedicated tier entitlements + explicit exclusions (burst, failover, misuse)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Dedicated Throughput SLO + Tiered Capacity (2025 H1)
description:
Goal
- Lock tier entitlements (burst + failover posture) and produce an explicit exclusions list that can be reused across:
  1) customer-facing docs (Dedicated tiers overview)
  2) order form / MSA addendum SLO language
  3) support escalation playbook
  4) sales enablement cheat sheet

Why now
- Sales/CS keep getting requests to “put the throughput guarantee in writing,” but we don’t have a consistent, non-gameable exclusions list.
- Infra/SRE need hard boundaries to operationalize routing/admission control without creating ambiguous customer expectations.

Scope
- Define entitlements per tier for:
  - Burst policy (how much, how long, how metered)
  - Failover posture (if any), and what is/isn’t considered an SLO miss
  - Support response targets related to throughput incidents (align w/ CS playbook)
- Define explicit exclusions that apply to the Dedicated throughput SLO measurement/reporting.

Out of scope
- Exact numeric throughput floors per shape/model (owned by PRD + shape catalog; referenced here only for wording).
- Implementation details of routing/admission control (ENG).

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/dedicated-throughput-slo-prd.json
- SLO formal definition: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-throughput-slo-definition.json
- ADR (canonical metric): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-027-throughput-slo-metric-definition.json
- Pricing tiers proposal: sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/dedicated-pricing-tiers-v1.json
- Sales cheat sheet: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pricing-guidance/dedicated-tier-cheat-sheet.json
- Escalation playbook: sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/dedicated-throughput-slo-escalation.json

Decision summary (final)

Tier entitlements (customer-facing)

1) Dedicated Standard
- Throughput commitment: “Committed throughput floor” for the configured deployment when running a Redwood-supported model+version on the contracted shape(s), measured per the Dedicated throughput SLO definition.
- Burst: Best-effort burst above committed throughput when capacity is available. Not guaranteed; may be rate-limited during fleet contention.
- Failover posture: No cross-region failover entitlement. In-region failover may occur for maintenance/hardware faults, but may impact latency/throughput temporarily.
- Support response target (throughput issues): business-hours initial response; on-call engagement if incident is confirmed and multi-tenant safety systems are involved.

2) Dedicated Plus
- Throughput commitment: Same committed throughput floor (written commitment) + tighter measurement/reporting cadence in Console.
- Burst: Included burst up to the tier-defined cap (expressed as % over committed) for short windows, subject to guardrails.
  - Burst definition: accepted requests above committed throughput are served opportunistically; burst consumption is metered and reported distinctly from committed.
  - If customer sustains above-burst traffic, admission control will shed/queue to protect the floor.
- Failover posture: In-region HA (spare capacity / warm pool) with automated failover within region for node failures. No cross-region throughput guarantee.
- Support response target: 24x7 for confirmed SLO-impacting incidents; faster escalation path to SRE/Infra.

3) Dedicated Premium
- Throughput commitment: Highest committed throughput floor + most restrictive variance band (i.e., most conservative sizing and headroom).
- Burst: Included burst at higher cap and longer allowed windows compared to Plus; still subject to overload protection.
- Failover posture:
  - In-region HA with warm pool required.
  - Optional cross-AZ redundancy where supported by the shape/region.
  - If cross-region failover is purchased as an add-on, it is explicitly scoped as “disaster recovery failover” with separate RTO/RPO-style terms; not counted toward the primary region throughput SLO while failed over unless explicitly stated.
- Support response target: 24x7 with highest priority paging; dedicated incident comms cadence and named escalation contacts.

Notes on burst (wording constraints)
- We will NOT promise “unlimited burst” in any tier.
- We will NOT define burst in terms of tokens/sec guarantee; it remains “included and metered above committed” with clear caps and overload behavior.
- Burst being “included” means: billed/charged per pricing policy but not treated as SLO obligation.

Exclusions (applies to throughput SLO eligibility)

A request/time window may be excluded from SLO calculations (and remedies/credits) when throughput shortfall is attributable to any of the below:

A) Customer-side throttling / backpressure / client behavior
- Customer-configured client-side rate limits, concurrency caps, or backoff policies preventing reaching committed throughput.
- Upstream dependency bottlenecks (e.g., customer gateway, VPC egress, or app server constraints) that reduce delivered QPS.
- Customer request patterns that cause self-inflicted queueing (e.g., highly spiky traffic with long idle periods that repeatedly triggers cold/warm transitions when warm pool is not purchased).

B) Unsupported models, versions, or non-conforming deployment configuration
- Use of models/versions not listed as “Supported for Dedicated SLO” for that shape/region.
- Switching models/versions without Redwood-supported rollout process (e.g., customer pins to a model variant outside the contracted perf profile).
- Running outside published limits for the contracted shape (e.g., max context, max batch, max output tokens) where Redwood has stated performance is variable.
- Use of experimental/preview model features marked “best effort” (e.g., non-default quant profiles, experimental kernels) unless explicitly included in the order form.

C) Misuse patterns / intentionally adversarial or pathological workloads
- Prompting patterns that create extreme variance or sustained worst-case compute (e.g., consistently max output tokens + long contexts) beyond what was sized/contracted.
- Automated traffic that is predominantly invalid/failed requests (4xx) or retries due to customer integration issues.
- Abuse, load testing, benchmarking, or synthetic traffic not coordinated with Redwood (unless explicitly approved in writing), especially if it exceeds admission control limits.

D) Shared responsibility items outside Redwood control
- Customer network/VPN misconfiguration (for VPC-connected Dedicated) that introduces packet loss/latency leading to reduced effective throughput.
- Customer-managed DNS/CDN/service mesh issues.

E) Maintenance / force majeure / planned events
- Scheduled maintenance windows communicated per contract (only the communicated window is excluded; unplanned overrun is not excluded).
- Force majeure and third-party cloud outages per standard MSA language.

F) Measurement exclusions / instrumentation integrity
- Known measurement anomalies acknowledged by Redwood (e.g., metric pipeline delays or accounting bugs) where we will re-compute and publish corrected SLO results.
- Partial outages in customer-provided telemetry integrations (if used as a secondary signal) do not qualify as SLO misses.

Customer-facing phrasing draft (for PM-503)
- “Committed throughput applies when the Dedicated deployment is configured according to Redwood’s supported model/version and shape guidance. Throughput may vary with request mix (context length, output length, streaming, tool use). Redwood may exclude periods where performance is limited by customer-side throttling, unsupported configurations, or misuse patterns. Burst capacity is provided subject to availability and overload protection and is not part of the committed throughput guarantee.”

Acceptance criteria
- Tier entitlements (burst + failover posture) are reflected consistently in:
  - dedicated-pricing-tiers-v1.json (packaging)
  - dedicated-tier-cheat-sheet.json (sales)
  - dedicated-throughput-slo-definition.json (SRE exclusions alignment)
  - dedicated-throughput-slo-escalation.json (CS playbook)
- Exclusions list is reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael), Infra (Irene/Vanessa), Support (Dev Patel/Rachel Kim), and Legal (Sofia Mendes) and approved for use in customer-facing SLO language.

Rollout notes
- Standard: ship first with conservative wording; Plus/Premium: require Legal signoff for “written commitment” language and remedies.
- Ensure Console terminology uses the same words: “Committed throughput” vs “Burst usage.”

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Do we offer cross-region failover as a default Premium entitlement?
  - A: No. Cross-region is an explicit add-on with separate terms; do not imply throughput SLO continues while failed over.
- Q: Is burst ever SLO-covered?
  - A: No; burst is metered and best-effort beyond committed.

Follow-ups
- PM-503: incorporate the customer-facing language draft and exclusions into order form / public docs.
- PM-497: ensure pricing includes burst caps and warm pool/HA requirements by tier.
- Support enablement: update macros to reference the exclusions list verbatim (avoid re-phrasing per agent).
comments: 2025-02-20 (Lauren Bishop): Drafted initial exclusions list based on SRE metric exploration notes + recent Support tickets (streaming double-counting + burst confusion). Requesting SRE/Infra review for any “gameable” gaps.

2025-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): +1 on explicitly excluding customer-side throttles and unsupported model versions. Recommend we tie eligibility to “Supported for Dedicated SLO” metadata in model catalog so it’s objectively checkable.

2025-02-24 (Irene Choi): Please call out warm pool requirement for Premium HA posture; otherwise customers will expect instant recovery after idle. Also clarify that long-idle/cold start is not an SLO miss unless warm pool purchased.

2025-02-25 (Rafael Mendes): We should avoid exclusions that require subjective interpretation. Prefer: (a) config eligibility checks (model/version/shape), (b) explicit request limits (max ctx/output), (c) customer-side rate limiting evidence. Everything else should fall back to incident review.

2025-02-26 (Laura Bennett): Finance needs burst to be explicitly not-guaranteed and excluded from remedies; otherwise customers will push for credits based on “we were bursting last week and now we can’t.” Wording updated to make burst “included and metered, not committed.”

2025-02-27 (Sofia Mendes): Legal ask: keep force majeure / third-party outage language consistent with standard MSA. Also ensure we don’t promise cross-region failover unless purchased. Added explicit DR add-on carveout under Premium.

2025-03-03 (Dev Patel): Support request: make the exclusions list copy/pasteable into escalation responses and the status page template. Also add an item for “synthetic load tests not coordinated with Redwood.” Added under Misuse patterns.

2025-03-06 (Lauren Bishop): Marking done. Final wording synced to pricing tiers + cheat sheet drafts; PM-503 will carry customer-facing contract language and remedies. Shared final exclusions in #sales and #customer-success for enablement.
